subject.title: fix(gateway): bound BOOT.md file read size

question: Should the BOOT.md size-cap fix preserve current symlink-following behavior, or should BOOT.md become regular-file-only as an intentional security hardening?
rationale: The memory bound is clearly useful, but choosing `readRegularFile` also changes an existing filesystem behavior that could affect real workspaces; automation should not decide that compatibility/security tradeoff silently.

options.title: Preserve current symlink behavior
options.body: Keep this PR focused on bounding memory use, and handle regular-file-only BOOT.md as a separate hardening change if maintainers want it.

options.title: Accept regular-file-only BOOT.md
options.body: Treat symlink rejection as intended hardening, then require explicit coverage and release-note context for the compatibility break.

recommendation.title: Preserve current symlink behavior
recommendation.body: Keep this PR focused on bounding memory use, and handle regular-file-only BOOT.md as a separate hardening change if maintainers want it.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original BOOT.md feature and recent BOOT.md safety work, making him the best available routing owner for the compatibility/security choice.
